notes: Trade-association summary of a Rwanda Development Board / Visit Rwanda TV broadcast, not a direct interview; the page carries a 2026-02-03 publication timestamp. Executives are not named here. Deli Box Rwanda was not found elsewhere (searched: Deli Box Rwanda Kigali).

claim: A 2018 trade-press report (based on a KT Press tour of the Rwanda-Israel Horticulture Center of Excellence at Mulindi) says high-end hotels in Rwanda 'have complained about poor quality of local fruits and vegetables - pushing them to import the products'; the claim is unattributed and the article gives no figures.
title: Rwanda-Israel horticulture deal to cut down on imports
notes: Eight years old and unattributed; used only as a lead on hotel quality complaints, not as a measure of import share (no import-share study was found).

claim: In March 2026 anonymous restaurant operators and a Kigali butchery owner said input costs were rising and quickly passed into menu prices; imported items include certain meats, seafood, spices, oils and beverages; a Kimironko Market worker said chicken and goat meat had become more expensive; the butchery owner said 'Sometimes we buy meat at higher prices and we have to sell at a small margin'; the article says the government aims to strengthen links between farmers, processors, urban markets and hospitality businesses and that some restaurants are adding domestic products to menus; no meat or fruit price figures are given.
title: Is dining out in Kigali becoming too expensive?
notes: Businesses are not named; the Rwanda Hospitality Association chairman is quoted by name in the article (not used here).

claim: After RURA raised pump prices (petrol RWF1,989 to 2,303 per litre and diesel RWF1,948 to 2,205, effective 2026-04-04), a Gisimenti (Kigali) fruit vendor reported higher fruit prices and transport per sack doubling from RWF1,000 to 2,000: mangoes imported from Kenya RWF900-1,000 each (from 600-700), oranges RWF1,200 per kilo (from 700), watermelons from Tanzania and Uganda, apples from South Africa RWF160,000 a box (from about 86,000); suppliers 'attribute the rise mainly to higher transport costs'.
title: Rwanda produce prices rise on higher fuel costs
notes: Retail vendor prices at one Kigali hub; USD equivalents in the article not used. Shows imported fruit on Kigali stalls in 2026 and a transport-cost shock.

claim: Irembo livestock relocation service: lets citizens relocate livestock between sectors and districts within Rwanda; sector veterinary authorities approve moves within a sector and district veterinary authorities oversee district-to-district moves; applicant needs an ID and a phone or email; application on irembo.gov.rw under Agriculture and Livestock; free of charge; processing time 3 days; certificate downloaded after approval; no goat- or sheep-specific conditions listed.
title: How to apply for livestock relocation
notes: Date is the page's 'Modified on' stamp. The page does not mention the 2026 Rift Valley fever quarantine, so whether certificates are issued for quarantined areas is unknown.

claim: Explainer on setting up an abattoir: meat businesses that slaughter, transport or sell unprocessed meat must register with RICA and obtain a licence before using facilities; slaughter only in designated areas of slaughterhouse premises (not homes or bush); meat handlers need medical certificates every six months; RICA technical regulation N DGO/REG/003 of 2022-04-25 (Articles 54-65) sets sanitary, traceability, infrastructure and equipment requirements for retail shops and abattoirs.
title: Explainer: Nine things to know about setting up an abattoir in Rwanda
notes: URL is exactly as returned by search but its slug opens an unrelated 2009 article when fetched; claims are taken from the search engine's excerpt and the Irembo slaughterhouse-licence page it points to returned HTTP 404. Verify with RICA before relying on it.

claim: In September 2025 a trade summary (quoting Food Business Africa) described Kigali's supermarket landscape as dominated by local and regional operators: Simba Supermarket with 13 branches, Sawa Citi (shifting to the SPAR format, rebranding all its stores), the centrally located 2000 Supermarket, and Sharma Supermarket (imported specialty goods); Coopérative U planned at least 10 Rwandan stores over five years with a U Express at Inzovu Mall in early 2026; Rwanda would be its 11th African market.
title: French-based 'U' supermarket and hypermarket brand opening in Rwanda
notes: Simba's branch count here (13) is below the 15 reported by the New Times in August 2026 (BUY-01); the difference may be growth. Nakumatt and Uchumi are not named among current operators.

claim: Afri-Farmers Market online price list on 2026-10-19 (retail; items 'Sold By: All Branches'): passion fruits RWF3,800/kg, yellow passion RWF3,000/kg, tree tomatoes RWF3,000/kg, mangoes RWF3,000/kg, Hass avocado RWF2,000/kg, avocado RWF700 each, pineapple RWF2,200 each, papaya RWF2,200 each, local oranges RWF2,000/kg, lemons RWF2,000/kg, mandarin RWF3,000/kg; fresh-meat category lists beef, chicken, fish and eggs (beef fillet RWF17,000/kg, beef steak RWF10,000/kg, chicken legs RWF9,500/kg); none of the roughly 20 meat-category items read was goat or sheep.
title: Afri-Farmers Market: Fresh Fruit and Fresh Meat categories (product pages)
